extracted.intended_audience: contributors and editors of ProofWiki (mathematical page authors)
extracted.subtask_description: House-style and LaTeX/source-code conventions for composing, formatting, and linking mathematical pages and proofs on the ProofWiki site. Covers equation templates, symbol usage, linguistic style, linking, and other editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: House style mastery and editing workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Active contributors are expected to gradually master the house style; when first starting, seasoned editors will tidy pages you write or create.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are encouraged to study the changes made and pick up the style as you progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to Theorems and Axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a theorem is invoked or referred to, it should be referenced by its full title; for axioms use the Axiom-link template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the page title between double square brackets (e.g. [[Union Distributes over Intersection]]). For axioms, use the Axiom template: {{Axiom-link|Choice}} producing 'Axiom of Choice'. No need to change case of theorem names.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a concept (or part of it) is invoked on a page, it should be presented as a link to the definition of that concept; preferred that every use of the word be linked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer linking to the top-level Definition page (e.g. Definition:Prime Number) rather than subpages unless a specific instance is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent redirects to subpage definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If definitions have subpages (e.g. Definition:Primitive (Calculus)/Real) there ought to be a permanent redirect to the appropriate page which should be used in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is none, feel free to implement a permanent redirect; do not invoke individual subpages unless necessary to avoid circularity or to handle multiple definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical symbols allowed in source
rubrics_metrics.description: Only standard alphanumeric and punctuation characters found on a standard English-language keyboard are accepted in LaTeX source code; letters with diacritics should not be used directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-English characters (e.g. Greek) are needed, use the full LaTeX command such as \alpha. Avoid inserting literal non-keyboard characters into source except when reporting mathematician names or in language notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline equations markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline equations merely need the dollar delimiters ($...$).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The semilinear wave equation $\partial_t U = A U + \map B U$ is written with $...$.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed equations formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Displayed equations should be indented using a single colon, not centered with $$ ... $$ which is discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of preferred input: :$\ds \map H U = \int_0^{2\pi} ...$ . Centering with $$E = m c^2$$ is discouraged as it breaks short-sentence house style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \ds for big operators
rubrics_metrics.description: The \ds command should be used at the front of expressions using big operators such as \sum, \prod, \frac, \lim, \bigcup, \bigcap, \int etc., whether displayed or inline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n, \ds \frac {-b \pm \sqrt{...}}{2 a}. Use \mathop to enforce spacing for = and \in when used in subscripts of big operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated big-operator symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain symbols have abbreviated forms for their big versions: \dfrac can be used instead of \ds \frac and \dbinom instead of \ds \binom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using \dfrac and \dbinom inside a line defined as \ds is harmless and can aid refactoring; use consistently if preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: The roman 'd' in calculus
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing calculus operators, use a non-italic (roman) form for the d by writing \d or \rd (the latter includes a half-space before it for integrals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer \dfrac{\d y}{\d x} (source) rather than \dfrac{d y}{d x} which renders an italic d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use available fonts with their conventional mathematical roles: \mathcal (calligraphy), \mathbb or \Bbb (blackboard), \mathscr (script), \mathsf (sans), \mathfrak (fraktur), \mathtt (fixed width).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of Fraktur and Script is discouraged for readability. \T and \F implemented for True and False; standard sets \N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C have their own codes. All \mathcal uppercase letters have shortcuts like \AA, \BB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of logical symbols in exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using logic symbols \land and \lor in general mathematical exposition because they can be ambiguous outside logic; prefer writing words 'and' and 'or'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve \land and \lor for their use in the field of logic; in algebra or set theory write 'and'/'or' to avoid reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation with displayed equations
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence broken by a displayed equation should be ended with a colon; the displayed equation itself should not be ended with a full stop or comma and punctuation should appear outside the LaTeX environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the full stop inside the LaTeX that terminates an equation. Correct: Hence: $\displaystyle ...$ (no trailing period inside LaTeX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of QED templates
rubrics_metrics.description: To end a proof, use the {{qed}} template which yields a black square (\blacksquare); for subproofs use {{qed|lemma}} which yields a hollow box (\Box).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the template immediately after the last line of the proof (i.e. on the next line), not separated by blank lines. Do not write 'Q.E.D.' — it's discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX code spacing and syntax style
rubrics_metrics.description: Source-code conventions: each variable and each command beginning with a backslash should be preceded by a space (except when enclosing things in brackets). When enclosing brackets, use \paren{...} rather than literal parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using \big, \Big, etc.; prefer \paren{...} for sizing. Put punctuation outside math environment. Single-character parameters need not be in braces: \dfrac 1 2 preferred to \dfrac {1} {2}; but maintain spacing conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive sizing commands
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be no need to use the commands \big, \Big, \Bigg etc.; using \paren{...} will almost always automatically size parentheses aesthetically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \paren{...} instead of manual size commands for cleaner and maintainable source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aligned equations templates and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the begin-eqn, eqn, end-eqn templates to create aligned equations; each equality/inequality should be on a new line and the environment is already in \displaystyle mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure: {{begin-eqn}} {{eqn | l = ... | r = ... }} ... {{end-eqn}}. | l = contains left environment, | r = right. | c = is for comments (not a LaTeX environment). Omit empty columns; align pipes and equals signs for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eqn-template caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include two consecutive open or close curly braces '{{' or '}}' anywhere in your {{eqn}} templates, and do not include the vertical bar '|' in LaTeX expressions inside the eqn environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spaces between braces (e.g. '{ {') to avoid interpreter breakage. Use \vert or \lvert/\rvert instead of '|' and \Vert instead of '\|'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aligned material column behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The | c = section of an eqn template is not a LaTeX environment and should be used to add comments about the equation; it often holds a link or a label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use | ll = and | rr = for additional columns if needed; the ll column is often used for 'implies' or 'leads to' signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each sentence should be short and linear
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sentence should be short and should convey one step: either one simple statement or one compound statement of form 'P, therefore Q'. Each sentence should be on a separate line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer short-line style: 'Let P hold. From Fred's Theorem, it follows that Q.' Avoid long chained sentences with multiple nested reasons in one sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid parenthetical notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid sliding further information into the middle of a sentence via parentheses; parenthetical material often causes confusion when it contains mathematical notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional material is needed, present it as a separate sentence or phrase. Do not overuse parentheses in proofs or definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid filler words and waffle
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include empty statements that do not impart information (e.g., 'The first part of the proof is easy.', 'This article is complete as far as it goes...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use templates like {{handwaving}} and {{explain}} where appropriate; avoid generic 'You can help...' or meta-statements that add no content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization after displayed math continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a sentence continues after a displayed mathematical expression, do not start the continuation clause with a capital letter; it is a continuation of the same sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Let: $\ds S = ...$ where $\ds \sum$ denotes summation. The 'where' should be lowercase because it continues the sentence that began before the display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer terse phrasing; avoid ambiguous 'any'
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'any' can be ambiguous and is discouraged; consider using 'every' or 'an arbitrary' instead to improve clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose wording that makes quantification explicit; prefer terseness but clarity and completeness override terseness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abbreviations like 'e.g.' and 'i.e.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations such as 'e.g.' and 'i.e.' are discouraged due to common misuse; also beware confusion between 'its' and 'it's'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full phrases (for example / that is) to remove ambiguity; prefer 'it is' over 'it's' in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and naming in definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In definitions, prefer simple linguistic forms (e.g., 'X is some object') rather than verbose phrases like 'X is called' or 'X is known as'; use 'is' to state definitions directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep definition phrasing concise: 'X is some object.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking policy and internal reference rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure ease of reference and consistency, the rules for internal references must be adhered to: linkorems, axioms, and definitions as specified; see the 'this section' on creating links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal links liberally for concepts that have their own pages; refer to templates and tools like 'What links here' to find redirects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of templates for examples and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use designated templates (e.g., {{Defof}}, {{Eqn}}, {{qed}}) to streamline presentation and maintain consistent house style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: {{Defof}} is designed for the c parameter of the Eqn template and not for general body exposition because it starts with a capital letter; use appropriate templates in the correct contexts.
